transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-03-26 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~47 minutes
Attendees: Alicia Park (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Karen Liu (Helio - Head of ML Ops), Tom Reyes (Helio - Platform Eng), Priya Nayar (Helio - Security)
Recording link: https://app.fireflies.ai/recordings/ff-20260326-pt-7893 (internal)
Shared artifacts: 1) POC runbook deck - https://redwood.app/s/helio-poc-deck, 2) Incident logs (redacted) - drive/helio/poc_logs, 3) Retry config sample - link in chat

[00:00] Alicia: alright good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. this is our weekly poc sync, focusing on the reliability incident you saw last thursday. um Samir and I will walk through what we observed and figure out next steps. Karen, do you want to start with a quick recap of what you saw on your side?
[00:22] Karen: yeah sure, thanks. so last thursday between 09:10 and 09:45 our app saw a spike of timeouts and about 0.6% 5xx errors hitting the redwood endpoint. most of the 5xx are 502/504-ish. the client reported increased latency p95 crossing 2.5s from a baseline of ~600ms. we routed traffic through our Envoy layer, and saw connection resets.
[00:44] Tom: and to add, our traffic spiked due to a batch job being kicked off, we had a sequence of short bursts - not a steady sustained increase but a couple of high QPS bursts. we also saw threadpool saturation on our side for a bit.
[01:05] Samir: ok, thanks. from Redwood telemetry, we saw corresponding backend queueing on the dedicated pool during the same window. there were a handful of overloaded worker restarts and some transient k8s pod restarts, which correlates to a small window where requests queued and hit upstream timeouts.
[01:28] Priya: quick question, are the ingress timeouts set to what the default is? because we use pretty low client timeouts so the user sees a failure quickly.
[01:36] Alicia: good question. we documented the recommended timeouts in the runbook. but yeah, sometimes client timeouts + aggressive retries can amplify bursts.
[01:48] Karen: we were using our standard 1.5s deadline in Envoy to Redwood and we do have a retry policy in front but it's conservative.
[01:56] Samir: two quick hypotheses: one is queueing on the dedicated pool due to bursty arrivals + small worker count (we saw p95/p99 upwards), second is connection pool exhaustion at Envoy causing resets; lastly a mismatch between upstream idle timeout and client deadlines which surfaces as 504s.
[02:20] Tom: can you show the traces that tie the requests from our request id into your worker logs? we tried to match but saw id mismatches sometimes.
[02:30] Samir: yes, we have the correlating request_id in the logs. we'll share aggregated p95/p99 traces with the request ids for the incident window. we think some of the request ids were trimmed by your proxy or truncated in transit causing matching issues.
[02:46] Karen: ok, that explains some of the mismatch. also we saw increased 429 throttles around the same time - are these from your rate limits?
[02:54] Alicia: there are a couple of layers: host-level rate limits on the hosted product and per-customer throttles on the dedicated config. we didn't see wholesale rate-limiting across the pool but your spike did push up internal throttles in one AZ which caused some 429s that cascaded to retries.
[03:12] Priya: from a security/compliance pov we need to capture audit logs for every 5xx and have redwood mark which requests hit protected PII payloads - will you be able to share redacted audit logs?
[03:23] Alicia: yes, we can share redacted logs. Samir will extract the relevant fields and we can redact with request ids but not raw payloads.
[03:33] Samir: i'll include timestamp, request_id, route, response_code, worker_id, and the kernel-level trace snippet - redacted.
[03:43] Karen: perfect.

[04:00] Samir: going back to mitigations: short term we recommend three conservative changes - 1) temporarily increase dedicated pool worker count/capacity to smooth bursts, 2) tweak Envoy connection pool & idle timeout to avoid connection churn, 3) apply client-side retry/backoff with jitter and capped retries to avoid retry storms.
[04:24] Tom: for (1) how fast can you scale the dedicated pool? we have a hard window of peak in the morning and we need faster ramp.
[04:31] Samir: autoscale is enabled but by default it reacts based on CPU/queue depth over a minute or two. we can provision burst capacity for the pilot - a reserved buffer that can absorb short bursts immediately. that requires a config change and we can enable it quickly for your workspace.
[04:47] Karen: cost impact?
[04:50] Alicia: there will be incremental cost for burst buffer, we can provide an estimate. for the pilot we can enable a small buffer and monitor.

[05:05] Tom: for the retry guidance, we've had bad experiences with exponential backoff causing more downstream load; what are you recommending exactly?
[05:14] Samir: recommend max 2 retries, initial backoff 150-250ms with jitter, and a per-request overall deadline of 3s. also ensure idempotency where possible. we'll send you an example Envoy config and a client library snippet.
[05:29] Priya: can the Redwood client surface non-retriable error codes so we can short-circuit retries for certain 4xx/5xx?
[05:36] Samir: yes, we return structured error codes and a retriable boolean in the API response wrapper in the SDK. if using plain REST you can check the error code mapping in the runbook.

[06:05] Alicia: ok let's walk through the incident timeline as we see it in our observability - Samir do you have the p99 traces up?
[06:13] Samir: yep, share screen - so at 09:11 we see a spike in incoming QPS, by 09:12 queue depth increases on the worker and p99 token generation latency jumps. by 09:14 we have a few worker restarts due to OOM on a noisy model variant, a short burst of 502s while the pool stabilizes. around 09:17 we see Envoy connection resets correlating to low ephemeral ports on your Envoy side.
[06:41] Tom: we also saw our node pool auto-restart due to CPU thrash on the client side, so there was some overlap.
[06:50] Samir: yes, this overlap amplified the end-user impact. the main takeaway: it's multi-factor - both sides had constrained resources during the spike.

[07:10] Karen: for the OOMs you mentioned on your side, what's the cause? model variant memory pressure? configuration?
[07:18] Samir: looks like a specific model variant used by one route had higher tensor size for longer sequences; combined with the bursty batch packing it triggered memory pressure. we have a mitigation: pin to a lower-memory variant for the pilot or enable a memory-based autoscaler threshold which evicts long requests faster.
[07:36] Alicia: that is a tradeoff with latency/quality - pinning to lower-memory will lower p95 slightly maybe. we should weigh that vs user-perceived errors.

[07:50] Priya: from compliance, we need explicit retention windows for logs and an audit trail of who accessed them. is that supported for the pilot?
[07:58] Alicia: yes, audit logs are available for Dedicated/Private with configurable retention; we'll attach the retention policy doc. for this POC we can provide 90-day redacted logs.

[08:15] Karen: what about the 429s - you said internal throttles in one AZ. can we disable throttles for the pilot?
[08:22] Samir: we can raise your per-customer soft-limit for the pilot, effectively preventing throttles until a higher threshold. it's not recommended unlimited, but for controlled tests we can lift it.

[08:34] Tom: ok, so immediate plan: 1) Redwood increases worker buffer and raises per-customer throttles for pilot, 2) customer adjusts Envoy pool/timeouts and applies recommended retry config, 3) both sides capture full traces/logs for the incident window and share. is that correct?
[08:50] Alicia: yes. adding: Redwood will also temporarily pin the problematic route to the lower-memory variant while we tune batching and quantization settings.

[09:05] Karen: on the traces, can you include the full request path and model variant? that'll help us correlate which route caused the OOMs.
[09:12] Samir: yes we'll include route, model_variant, request_id, server_worker, and timestamp.

[09:22] Alicia: timeline and owners: Samir will deliver logs/traces by Friday (2026-03-28), Alicia will share cost delta for the burst buffer, Tom/Karen will plan the 24h spike test and send schedule by EOD Monday (2026-03-30).

[09:45] Priya: one more question on retries - if we put the retry in the client layer, how do we avoid duplicate side-effects? our endpoints are not fully idempotent.
[09:54] Samir: best practice is to put a small unique idempotency key on requests that mutate state; for non-idempotent calls consider server-side de-dup within your app. for inference-only calls, retries are fine with bounded retries.

[10:12] Tom: are there any config knobs on Redwood to reduce tail latency besides scaling? like quantization/serve-time optimizations?
[10:20] Samir: yes - we have quantized variants, and we can adjust batching windows and KV cache behavior to reduce per-request compute. for short bursts, reducing batch wait time can help tail latency but may increase per-token cost. we'll provide a tradeoff table.

[10:40] Karen: also noticed some transcription mismatches in the logs where request ids get hyphenated differently. is there a canonical request id format we should enforce?
[10:48] Samir: we emit UUID4-like request IDs; some proxies rewrite or truncate. we'll recommend preserving the header x-request-id and not performing character sanitization. we'll put that note in the runbook.

[11:05] Alicia: ok let's talk tests: Karen/Tom can you run a 24h spike test that simulates your batch job pattern? we want both the short bursts and the baseline traffic. please include retries toggled on/off to validate amplification risk.
[11:20] Karen: yes we can. we'll also run a version with a higher timeout and one with the shorter timeout to compare user impact.

[11:33] Tom: we might need a small change on the client side to add an idempotency key and adjust connection pool settings - will take us a day.

[11:42] Priya: any security approval needed for sharing traces? we'll need an NDA addendum for full logs if payloads are involved.

[11:49] Alicia: for raw payloads we will require the NDA addendum; for redacted traces it's covered by the existing pilot agreement. we'll send the addendum if needed.

[12:00] Samir: i'll call out the exact format of the logs in the ticket - CSV + gzipped JSONL with request_id index.

[12:10] Alicia: recap - action items and owners (we'll post these in CRM): 1) Samir - share logs/traces (2026-03-28), 2) Alicia - cost estimate for burst buffer (2026-03-28), 3) Samir - example retry/backoff and Envoy config (2026-03-29), 4) Karen/Tom - schedule and run 24h spike test (start by 2026-04-01, results by 2026-04-02), 5) Priya - confirm NDA addendum if they want raw payloads.

[12:45] Karen: sounds good. do you want a follow-up deep dive with infra next week?
[12:49] Alicia: yes let's schedule the infra deep-dive with your SREs and our runtime team week of 2026-03-30, 45-60 minute slot.

[13:00] Tom: one last item - can you temporarily route our pilot traffic to a single AZ to simplify debugging?
[13:07] Samir: yes we can pin AZ for a limited window; will require a short maintenance window but doable.

[13:20] Alicia: great. thanks everyone. we'll send notes and the artifacts. any other questions?
[13:26] Priya: none here.
[13:28] Karen: nope, thanks.
[13:30] Alicia: thanks all, see you next week. bye.

(Transcript ends - timestamps approximate; occasional transcription errors and filler words present)
